text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a p99 tail bump on the continuous-batcher node group after last night's prefetch tweak. Anyone else seeing this?

samir: yep, saw the spike. p99 up ~30ms for small requests on batchers-v2 after the rollout :thinking: 

maya: logs point to more join-waits. small reqs are sometimes sitting behind a large request that holds the slot.

jin: did we change max_prefetch from 3 -> 5 in that rollout?

elena: we did — the idea was to improve fill rate for medium requests. it increases headroom but also lengthens coalesce windows.

maya: here's an example from the logs showing the delay pattern:
```
enqueue: request_id=abc123 size_tokens=12 prefetch=5
batch_wait=18ms held_by=request_large_efg
```

samir: so tradeoff = better throughput for medium batches vs higher variance for tiny fast requests. maybe we should try soft_reserve for small routes instead of global prefetch bump.

elena: soft_reserve would let tiny fast requests skip the deeper prefetch queue. also we could propagate deadline_hint from API to admission to prefer low-latency requests.

ryan: we already surface "deadline_hint" in route config, but runtime isn't using it for admission decisions yet.

jin: alternative: make prefetch window adaptive — shrink it when p99 > SLO and expand when stable. cheap control loop based on recent tail.

opsbot: deploy-bot: rollout(prefetch-window=5) applied to cluster/batchers-v2 at 02:14 UTC.

maya: opsbot noted. immediate mitigation suggestion: rollback prefetch to 3 on the short-request shard to stop the regressions.

samir: +1 for rollback now. also let's add telemetry so root cause is clearer: batch_wait_by_size, batch_hold_cause, and prefetched_join_rate.

elena: I'll open a metrics PR to add those histograms and labels (tenant, size_bucket, hold_reason).

jin: we should also revisit eviction policy — frequent KV-cache evictions while prefetch is high could cause warmup spikes that amplify tail latency. maybe increase soft_ttl for hot tenants.

ryan: agree. evacuation + eviction churn is a multiplier. another option is a microfast lane: tiny fastpath queue that aggregates up to N tokens with timeout T so small requests never wait behind big ones.

samir: micro-lane is attractive but adds another queueing surface. we debated it before (complexity vs benefits). for now, adaptive prefetch + deadline-aware admission + better metrics seems like the lowest-risk path.

elena: action items: 1) metrics PR (elena) 2) rollback prefetch to 3 for short-route shard (samir) 3) jin prototype adaptive prefetch controller (prototype next week) 4) ryan configure fastpath routes + flag on-call watch.

maya: timeline? rollback now, metrics PR within 48h, prototype next week, revisit micro-lane if we still observe residual tail.

ryan: i'll assign on-call to monitor p50/p95/p99 for the shard and watch token-cost impact after rollback.

maya: thanks all :thumbsup: 

opsbot: alert-bot: rollback applied to cluster/batchers-v2-short at 02:38 UTC, monitoring for regressions.

opsbot: incident-bot: p99 returned to baseline within 12 minutes of rollback (auto-check).
